title: Flood-wind shared electrical class-template asset model

scope.purpose: Represent one facility-level generation interconnection substation once while showing reusable solar and wind bindings for flood-electrical damage modeling.

excluded_dimensions.reason: Site geometry elevations datums and flood exposure belong in a site-specific cell binding.
Project versus utility ownership is deliberately unresolved and must not be invented in a class template.
Contracts and insured inclusion require site evidence.
Component value allocation belongs in the governed cell crosswalk.
Outage and restoration consequences are downstream from direct physical damage.
This interchange describes class anatomy and dependency rather than a runtime risk result.

assumptions: The solar and wind entities illustrate alternative or hybrid consumers of one facility-level substation; they do not assert that every project contains both.
A standalone wind instantiation retains the wind entity and one facility-level substation rather than duplicating the GSU under the turbine fleet.
Solar and wind collection systems remain separate physical inventories even when a component response family can be shared.
The 2026-07-28 as_of_date is the model-build snapshot boundary only; it is not an observed source, event, operating, or relationship-effective date.
limitations: No observed site inventory geometry elevation owner contract value event or damage curve is represented.
The physical tree is the minimum flood-electrical decomposition and is not a complete substation bill of materials.
The model is a planning interchange and is not a runtime curve artifact or production database schema.
No real-world effective dates are known or implied; the timeless class-template serves relationships therefore use null start and end dates.

dimension_profiles.rationale: The model distinguishes the facility boundary from technology-specific generation assets.
Flood response and value must separate main transformer switchgear controls station service and terminations.
A facility-level substation can serve either technology without duplicating the physical object.
Expected template facts remain explicitly distinct from observed asset facts.
